nodes.statement: The new model is trained to match a \emph{pre-computed} regression target: \[ \mathrm{target}_\mathrm{exp}(x_0,x_1,s) = \tilde\beta^k_s(x_s,s,x_0) + h_r(x_0,x_1)\cdot \bigl(\dot I_s - \tilde\beta^k_s(x_s,s,x_0)\bigr), \] i.e.\ an explicit Euler step from the previous model toward $\dot I_s$ with step size $1+\log w_k$.
nodes.statement_short: Explicit Euler target from the previous model toward $\dot I_s$.
nodes.section: Q.2 CFM loss variants and the covariance update

nodes.name: Train by MSE
nodes.statement: The target is constructed without gradients and fixed before training begins, so the regression is one clean MSE step.
nodes.statement_short: Fit the new model by one MSE regression.
nodes.section: Q.2 CFM loss variants and the covariance update

nodes.name: Fixed-point target
nodes.statement: The exact weight $w_k = \exp(\log w_k)$ is retained, but the new model is trained to satisfy a \emph{fixed-point} condition. The regression target incorporates the current model prediction: \[ \mathrm{target}_\mathrm{imp}(x_0,x_1,s) = \tilde\beta^k_s(x_s,s,x_0) + w_k(x_0,x_1)\cdot \bigl(\dot I_s - \tilde\beta^{k+1}_s(x_s,s,x_0)\bigr). \]
nodes.statement_short: Target uses the new model's own prediction, defining a fixed point.
nodes.section: Q.2 CFM loss variants and the covariance update

nodes.name: Solve fixed point
nodes.statement: Solving for the fixed point gives $\tilde\beta^{k+1}_s = \bigl(\tilde\beta^k_s + w_k\,\dot I_s\bigr)/(1+w_k)$, a weighted average of the old field and the interpolant velocity.
nodes.statement_short: Closed-form fixed point is a weighted average of old field and $\dot I_s$.
nodes.section: Q.2 CFM loss variants and the covariance update

nodes.name: One stop-gradient step
nodes.statement: In practice the fixed point is approximated by one gradient step using a stop-gradient on the current model prediction.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate the fixed point with one stop-gradient update.
nodes.section: Q.2 CFM loss variants and the covariance update

nodes.name: Reduce to mu_t and define flow map
nodes.statement: We prove the bounds for $\mu_t$ (the case for $\nu_t$ follows identically using $v_t$ and $\nu_0$). Let $\Phi_t^u : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X}$ denote the flow map generated by the velocity field $u_t$, defined as the solution to the ODE: \[ \frac{d}{dt}\Phi_t^u(x) = u_t(\Phi_t^u(x)), \quad \Phi_0^u(x) = x. \]
nodes.statement_short: Treat $\mu_t$; introduce the flow map of $u_t$.
nodes.section: C Regularity of the Marginal Flows

nodes.name: Log-density along characteristics
nodes.statement:
By the continuity equation $\partial_t \mu_t + 
abla \cdot (\mu_t u_t) = 0$, the evolution of the log-density along the flow characteristics is governed by the negative divergence of the velocity field:  egin{equation}  rac{d}{dt} \log \mu_t(\Phi_t^u(x)) = -(
abla \cdot u_t)(\Phi_t^u(x)). \end{equation} Integrating \eqref{eq:log_density_ode} from $0$ to $t$ yields: \[ \log \mu_t(\Phi_t^u(x)) = \log \mu_0(x) - \int_0^t (
abla \cdot u_	au)(\Phi_	au^u(x)) \, d	au. \]
nodes.statement_short: Log-density evolves by minus the divergence; integrate.
nodes.section: C Regularity of the Marginal Flows

nodes.name: Uniform bounds
nodes.statement:
We now apply the uniform bounds from our assumptions: From Assumption ef{ass:initial_regularity}, $\|\log \mu_0\|_{C^2} \le C_{\mu 
u}$, which implies $\|\log \mu_0\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal{X})} \le C_{\mu 
u}$. From Assumption ef{ass:velocity_regularity}, $\sup_{	au} \|u_	au\|_{C^2} \le C_{\mathrm{uv}}$. This implies the divergence is bounded by $\|
abla \cdot u_	au\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal{X})} \le \|u_	au\|_{C^1} \le C_{\mathrm{uv}}$. Substituting these bounds into the integral equation: \[ \left| \log \mu_t(\Phi_t^u(x)) ight| \le \|\log \mu_0\|_\infty + \int_0^t \|
abla \cdot u_	au\|_\infty \, d	au \le C_{\mu 
u} + C_{\mathrm{uv}} \cdot t \le C_{\mu 
u} + C_{\mathrm{uv}}. \] Since $\Phi_t^u$ is a diffeomorphism on the compact domain $\mathcal{X}$ generated by a $C^2$ field, the map is surjective. Thus, for any $y \in \mathcal{X}$, there exists $x$ such that $y = \Phi_t^u(x)$, and the bound holds uniformly: \[ -(C_{\mu 
u} + C_{\mathrm{uv}}) \le \log \mu_t(y) \le (C_{\mu 
u} + C_{\mathrm{uv}}). \] Exponentiating these bounds, we explicitly define the constants: \[ C_{\mu}^{\min} := e^{-(C_{\mu 
u} + C_{\mathrm{uv}})}, \quad C_{\mu}^{\max} := e^{(C_{\mu 
u} + C_{\mathrm{uv}})}. \] The bounds $C_{
u}^{\min}, C_{
u}^{\max}$ are derived analogously using $
u_0$ and $v_t$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the integral by assumptions; surjectivity gives uniform two-sided bounds.
nodes.section: C Regularity of the Marginal Flows

nodes.name: Score regularity
nodes.statement:
Finally, regarding the spatial regularity of the score $
abla \log \mu_t$. By differentiating the relation $\mu_t(y) = \mu_0(x) \det(
abla \Phi_t^u(x))^{-1}$ (where $x = (\Phi_t^u)^{-1}(y)$), or equivalently differentiating the integral form, the gradient $
abla \log \mu_t$ involves $
abla \log \mu_0$, $
abla (	ext{div } u)$, and the Jacobian of the inverse flow $(\Phi_t^u)^{-1}$. Since $u \in C^2$ (Assumption ef{ass:velocity_regularity}) and $\log \mu_0 \in C^2$ (Assumption ef{ass:initial_regularity}), the flow map and its inverse are $C^2$ diffeomorphisms. Consequently, $
abla \log \mu_t$ remains bounded and Lipschitz continuous (i.e., $\log \mu_t \in C^2$).
nodes.statement_short: Flow map regularity gives bounded Lipschitz scores.
nodes.section: C Regularity of the Marginal Flows

nodes.name: Reduction to mu_t
nodes.statement: We prove both claims for $\mu_t$ (the arguments for $\nu_t$ follow identically).
nodes.statement_short: Treat $\mu_t$ only.
nodes.section: C Regularity of the Marginal Flows

nodes.name: Log-density is time-Lipschitz
nodes.statement:
extbf{Log-density is time-Lipschitz:} Dividing the continuity equation $\partial_t\mu_t + 
abla\cdot(\mu_t u_t)=0$ by $\mu_t > 0$ gives  egin{equation} \partial_t \log \mu_t = -
abla \cdot u_t - u_t \cdot 
abla \log \mu_t. \end{equation} By Assumption~ef{ass:velocity_regularity}, $\|
abla\cdot u_t\|_\infty \le C_{\mathrm{uv}}$ and $\|u_t\|_\infty \le C_{\mathrm{uv}}$. By Lemma~ef{lem:density_bounds}, $\|
abla\log\mu_t\|_\infty \le C_{\mathrm{score}} < \infty$ uniformly in $t$. Hence $\|\partial_t\log\mu_t\|_\infty \le C_{\mathrm{uv}}(1 + C_{\mathrm{score}}) =: L_{\log}$, and integrating over time yields the Lipschitz bound.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\partial_t\log\mu_t$ uniformly.
nodes.section: C Regularity of the Marginal Flows

nodes.name: Score is time-Lipschitz
nodes.statement:
extbf{Score is time-Lipschitz:} Let $s_t := 
abla\log\mu_t$. Taking the spatial gradient of \eqref{eq:log_density_time_deriv}:  egin{equation} \partial_t s_t = -
abla(
abla\cdot u_t) - J_{u_t}^T s_t - (
abla s_t)\,u_t, \end{equation} where $J_{u_t}$ is the Jacobian of $u_t$ and $
abla s_t = 
abla^2\log\mu_t$. By Assumption~ef{ass:velocity_regularity} ($u_t \in C^2$ uniformly) and Lemma~ef{lem:density_bounds} ($\log\mu_t \in C^2$ uniformly), all three terms on the right are bounded, giving $\|\partial_t s_t\|_\infty \le C$ for some uniform $C$. Integrating over time yields the second Lipschitz bound, defining $L_{\mathrm{score}} := \operatorname{ess\,sup}_{t\in[0,1]}\|\partial_t s_t\|_\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate in space and bound $\partial_t s_t$.
nodes.section: C Regularity of the Marginal Flows

nodes.name: Recall dynamics and marginal constraints
nodes.statement:
Recall $\pi_t\in\Pi(\mu_t,
u_t)$ evolve according to the infinitesimal tilting dynamics $\dot\pi_t(x,y)=\pi_t(x,y) ig(a_t(x)+b_t(y) ig)$, where $(a_t,b_t)$ are the infinitesimal tilting rates defined in \eqref{eq:def-a-b-path}. The marginal constraints $\pi_t\in\Pi(\mu_t,
u_t)$ read \[ \int_{\mathcal X} \pi_t(x,y)\,dy= \mu_t(x), \qquad \int_{\mathcal X} \pi_t(x,y)\,dx= 
u_t(y), \]
nodes.statement_short: Recall tilting dynamics and marginal constraints.
nodes.section: D Variational Characterization of the Tilting Dynamics

nodes.name: Differentiate constraints
nodes.statement: Differentiating in $t$ and using \eqref{eq:pi-dot} yields \[ \int \pi_t(x,y)\big(a_t(x)+b_t(y)\big)\,dy= \partial_t \mu_t(x), \qquad \int \pi_t(x,y)\big(a_t(x)+b_t(y)\big)\,dx= \partial_t \nu_t(y). \]
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate constraints in time.
nodes.section: D Variational Characterization of the Tilting Dynamics

nodes.name: Recall energy and duality
nodes.statement_short: Recall the energy; tower property gives duality of $T_t,S_t$.
nodes.section: D Variational Characterization of the Tilting Dynamics

nodes.name: Optimality conditions equal linear system
nodes.statement:
extbf{Optimality conditions $\Leftrightarrow$ linear system \eqref{eq:app_linear_system_ab}}: Consider the quadratic energy $\mathcal J_t$ defined above. Since $\mathcal J_t$ is a convex quadratic functional on $L^2(\mu_t)	imes L^2(
u_t)$, its minimizer is characterized by the vanishing of its Fr'echet derivatives. Let $p\in C^1(\mathcal X)$ be any arbitrary test function. Expanding $\mathcal J_t(a+\xi p,b)$ and differentiating at $\xi=0$ yields \[ \mathbb E_{\pi_t}\! ig[(a(X)+b(Y))\,p(X) ig] = \mathbb E_{\mu_t}\! ig[
abla p(X)\cdot u_t(X) ig]. \] By Lemma~ef{lem:ipp}, the right-hand side equals $\mathbb E_{\mu_t}[p(X)\,\zeta_t(X)]$ in weak form, where $\zeta_t=\partial_t\mu_t/\mu_t$. Using $\mathbb E_{\pi_t}[b(Y)p(X)]=\mathbb E_{\mu_t}[p(X)\,(T_t b)(X)]$, for all $p$, we obtain \[ \mathbb E_{\mu_t}\! ig[p(X)\,(a(X)+(T_t b)(X)-\zeta_t(X)) ig]=0, \] hence \[ a+T_t b=\zeta_t\qquad \mu_t	ext{-a.s.} \] An analogous argument with test functions depending only on $y$ gives, with $\eta_t=\partial_t
u_t/
u_t$, \[ b+S_t a=\eta_t\qquad 
u_t	ext{-a.s.} \] Therefore, the critical points of $\mathcal J_t$ are exactly the solutions of the linear system \[ a+T_t b=\zeta_t,\qquad b+S_t a=\eta_t, \] which is equivalent to \eqref{eq:app_linear_system_ab}.
nodes.statement_short: Frechet derivatives plus weak form give the linear system.
nodes.section: D Variational Characterization of the Tilting Dynamics

nodes.name: Existence and uniqueness modulo gauge
nodes.statement: \textbf{Existence and uniqueness modulo gauge:} The quadratic part of $\mathcal J_t$ is $\mathbb E_{\pi_t}[(a(X)+b(Y))^2]$, whose kernel consists precisely of constant gauges $(a,b)=(c,-c)$. Hence $\mathcal J_t$ is strictly convex on the quotient space modulo the gauge and admits a unique minimizer in each gauge class. Since $\mathcal J_t$ is a convex quadratic functional, this minimizer is characterized by the above linear system.
nodes.statement_short: Kernel of quadratic part is the gauge; strict convexity on the quotient.
nodes.section: D Variational Characterization of the Tilting Dynamics

nodes.name: Block coordinate descent and convergence
nodes.statement: \textbf{Block coordinate descent and convergence:} The associated block coordinate descent reads \[ a^{k+1}=\zeta_t-T_t b^{k}, \qquad b^{k+1}=\eta_t-S_t a^{k+1}. \] This scheme corresponds to a Gauss--Seidel iteration for the linear system \eqref{eq:app_linear_system_ab_TS}. To apply standard convergence results one works on the quotient space with the gauge fixed (e.g.\ $\int a\,d\mu_t=0$), on which $\mathcal{J}_t$ is strictly convex and the linear system is non-singular. Since $\mathcal J_t$ is a strictly convex quadratic functional (modulo the gauge), classical results on block coordinate descent for convex quadratic problems, or equivalently Gauss--Seidel methods for linear systems, ensure that the iterates decrease $\mathcal J_t$ monotonically and converge (modulo the gauge) to the unique minimizer; see, e.g., \cite{bertsekas1997nonlinear,tseng2001convergence}.
nodes.statement_short: Gauss-Seidel iteration converges to the unique minimizer.
nodes.section: D Variational Characterization of the Tilting Dynamics

nodes.name: Conditional expectation under tilted measure
nodes.statement: For a discrete step $\delta > 0$, the practical tilting update is defined by the density ratio $d\tilde{\pi}_{t+\delta}(x,y) \propto \exp(\delta(a_t(x)+b_t(y))) d\tilde{\pi}_t(x,y)$. By the definition of the conditional expectation, the updated vector field evaluates directly via integration: \begin{align*} \tilde{\beta}_s^{t+\delta}(z) = \mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\pi}_{t+\delta}}[\dot{I}_s \mid I_s = z] &= \frac{\int \dot{I}_s \exp(\delta(a_t(x)+b_t(y))) \delta(I_s - z) d\tilde{\pi}_t(x,y)}{\int \exp(\delta(a_t(x)+b_t(y))) \delta(I_s - z) d\tilde{\pi}_t(x,y)} \\ &= \frac{\mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\pi}_t}\!\left[ \dot{I}_s \exp(\delta(a_t(X)+b_t(Y))) \mid I_s=z \right]}{\mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\pi}_t}\!\left[ \exp(\delta(a_t(X)+b_t(Y))) \mid I_s=z \right]}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Write the tilted field as a weighted conditional expectation ratio.
nodes.section: E.1 Derivation of Algorithm A: Weighted CFM

nodes.name: Regression form
nodes.statement: Furthermore, since the conditional expectation $\mathbb{E}_{P}[Y \mid X]$ uniquely minimizes the mean squared error $\mathbb{E}_{P}[\|Y - f(X)\|^2]$, we can express the target as a regression objective. Applying the exact same change of measure, where the global normalization constant vanishes in the $\arg\min$: \begin{align*} \tilde{\beta}_s^{t+\delta} &= \arg\min_{\beta} \mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\pi}_{t+\delta}}\!\left[\|\dot{I}_s - \beta(I_s)\|^2\right] \\ &= \arg\min_{\beta} \mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\pi}_t}\!\left[\exp(\delta(a_t(X)+b_t(Y))) \|\dot{I}_s - \beta(I_s)\|^2\right], \end{align*} which rigorously yields the Weighted CFM objective \eqref{eq:weighted_cfm_lsq}.
nodes.statement_short: Conditional expectation minimizes MSE, giving the weighted regression.
nodes.section: E.1 Derivation of Algorithm A: Weighted CFM

nodes.name: Uniform bounds via Sinkhorn equations
nodes.statement: Fix $t \in [0,1]$. Marginalizing the relation $\pi_t(x,y) = \pi'(x,y) e^{\varphi_t(x) + \psi_t(y)}$ yields the fixed-point equations: \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \varphi_t(x) &= \log \mu_t(x) - \log \int_{\mathcal{X}} \pi'(x,y) e^{\psi_t(y)} dy, \\ \psi_t(y) &= \log \nu_t(y) - \log \int_{\mathcal{X}} \pi'(x,y) e^{\varphi_t(x)} dx. \end{aligned} \end{equation} By Lemma \ref{lem:density_bounds}, $\log \mu_t$ and $\log \nu_t$ are uniformly bounded. By Assumption \ref{ass:coupling_regularity}, the effective kernel $-\log \pi'$ is bounded. Viewing \eqref{eq:phipsi_sinkhorn} as standard EOT dual equations, these bounds directly guarantee uniform $L^\infty$ bounds for $\varphi_t$ and $\psi_t$ (e.g., Lemma 4.9 in \cite{nutz2021introduction}), establishing $C_{\infty}$.
nodes.statement_short: Fixed-point equations plus standard EOT bounds give sup bounds.
nodes.section: F.1 Uniform Boundedness via Relative Potentials

nodes.name: Lipschitz regularity
nodes.statement: For spatial regularity, differencing \eqref{eq:phipsi_sinkhorn} for any $x_1, x_2 \in \mathcal{X}$ gives: \begin{align*} |\varphi_t(x_1) - \varphi_t(x_2)| &\le |\log \mu_t(x_1) - \log \mu_t(x_2)| + \left| \log \frac{\int \pi'(x_1,y) e^{\psi_t(y)} dy}{\int \pi'(x_2,y) e^{\psi_t(y)} dy} \right|. \end{align*} By the 1-Lipschitz property of the Log-Sum-Exp operator, the second term is bounded by the term $\sup_y |\log \pi'(x_1,y) - \log \pi'(x_2,y)|$. Hence: \[ \mathrm{Lip}(\varphi_t) \le \mathrm{Lip}(\log \mu_t) + \mathrm{Lip}_{\mathcal{X}}(\log \pi'). \] From Lemma \ref{lem:density_bounds}, $\sup_{t \in [0,1]} \mathrm{Lip}(\log \mu_t) < \infty$ due to bounded scores. From Assumption \ref{ass:coupling_regularity}, $\mathrm{Lip}_{\mathcal{X}}(\log \pi') \le C_\mathrm{OT}$. Summing these provides the uniform Lipschitz constant $C_{\mathrm{Lip}}$ for $\varphi_t$. A symmetric argument applies to $\psi_t$.
nodes.statement_short: Log-sum-exp 1-Lipschitz yields Lipschitz constant.
nodes.section: F.1 Uniform Boundedness via Relative Potentials

nodes.name: Setup
nodes.statement: The relative dual potentials $(\varphi_t, \psi_t)$ satisfy the coupled Sinkhorn fixed-point equations as \eqref{eq:phipsi_sinkhorn}. We give the proof in two steps.
nodes.statement_short: Potentials satisfy Sinkhorn fixed-point equations; two steps.
nodes.section: F.1 Uniform Boundedness via Relative Potentials

nodes.name: Stability of the relative Sinkhorn operator
nodes.statement:
extbf{Stability of the relative Sinkhorn operator:} By Lemma ef{lem:temporal_marginal_regularity}, the marginal log-densities are Lipschitz continuous in time. Hence, there exists a uniform constant $L_{\log}$ such that for all $r, t \in [0,1]$:  egin{equation*} \|\log \mu_r - \log \mu_t\|_\infty \le L_{\log} |r - t|, \quad \|\log 
u_r - \log 
u_t\|_\infty \le L_{\log} |r - t|. \end{equation*} Let $\mathcal{O}_t$ be the composite operator such that $\psi_t = \mathcal{O}_t(\psi_t)$ defined using Sinkhorn's update \eqref{eq:phipsi_sinkhorn} for a fixed potential $\psi$:  egin{equation*} \mathcal{O}_t(\psi)(y) := \log 
u_t(y) - \log \int_{\mathcal{X}} \pi'(x,y) \exp \left( \log \mu_t(x) - \log \int_{\mathcal{X}} \pi'(x,z) e^{\psi(z)} dz ight) dx. \end{equation*} To quantify the temporal sensitivity of the operator, define the intermediate function $h(x, t) := \log \mu_t(x) - \log \int \pi'(x,z) e^{\psi(z)} dz$. For any fixed $\psi$, the difference between operators at times $r$ and $t$ satisfies:  egin{align*} |\mathcal{O}_r(\psi)(y) - \mathcal{O}_t(\psi)(y)| &\le |\log 
u_r(y) - \log 
u_t(y)| + \left| \log  rac{ \int \pi'(x,y) e^{h(x, r)} dx }{ \int \pi'(x,y) e^{h(x, t)} dx } ight|. \end{align*} By the 1-Lipschitz property of the Log-Sum-Exp operator, the second term is bounded by $\|h(\cdot, r) - h(\cdot, t)\|_\infty$. Since $\psi$ is fixed, the integral components in $h$ cancel out, leaving: \[ \|h(\cdot, r) - h(\cdot, t)\|_\infty = \|\log \mu_r - \log \mu_t\|_\infty. \] Combining this with Step 1, the operator perturbation is strictly bounded by:  egin{equation} \|\mathcal{O}_r(\psi) - \mathcal{O}_t(\psi)\|_\infty \le 2 L_{\log} |r - t|. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Operator perturbation in time bounded by $2L_{\log}|r-t|$.
nodes.section: F.1 Uniform Boundedness via Relative Potentials

nodes.name: Uniform contraction and fixed-point sensitivity
nodes.statement: \textbf{Uniform contraction and fixed-point sensitivity:} The operator $\mathcal{O}_t$ acts on the space of bounded functions. Under the Hilbert projective metric, the marginals $\mu_t, \nu_t$ act purely as pointwise translations, leaving the contraction rate unaffected. By Birkhoff's Theorem, the contraction ratio $\rho$ of $\mathcal{O}_t$ is determined \textit{exclusively} by the dynamic range of the strictly positive kernel $\pi'(x,y)$: \begin{equation*} \rho = \left( \frac{\sqrt{\Delta} - 1}{\sqrt{\Delta} + 1} \right)^2, \quad \text{where } \Delta = \exp\left( \sup_{x,y} \log \pi'(x,y) - \inf_{x,y} \log \pi'(x,y) \right). \end{equation*} By Assumption \ref{ass:coupling_regularity}, $\|\log \pi'\|_\infty \le C_\mathrm{OT}$, ensuring that $\Delta < \infty$. Consequently, $\rho < 1$ is a uniform constant for all $t \in [0,1]$. Let $\psi_r$ and $\psi_t$ be the fixed points of $\mathcal{O}_r$ and $\mathcal{O}_t$. By \eqref{eq:operator_perturbation}, utilizing the triangle inequality and the uniform contraction property: \begin{align*} \|\psi_r - \psi_t\|_\infty &\le \|\mathcal{O}_r(\psi_r) - \mathcal{O}_r(\psi_t)\|_\infty + \|\mathcal{O}_r(\psi_t) - \mathcal{O}_t(\psi_t)\|_\infty \\ &\le \rho \|\psi_r - \psi_t\|_\infty + 2 L_{\log} |r - t|. \end{align*} Rearranging yields $\|\psi_r - \psi_t\|_\infty \le \frac{2 L_{\log}}{1 - \rho} |r - t|$. By symmetry, the analogous bound holds for $\|\varphi_r - \varphi_t\|_\infty$. Since each individual potential is Lipschitz with constant $\frac{2L_{\log}}{1-\rho}$, their sum is bounded by $L_{\mathrm{pot}} := \frac{4 L_{\log}}{1 - \rho}$ (twice the individual constant) which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Birkhoff contraction plus perturbation gives fixed-point Lipschitz bound.
nodes.section: F.1 Uniform Boundedness via Relative Potentials

nodes.name: (i) Non-expansion
nodes.statement: (i) Since $\pi_t(\cdot \mid x)$ is a valid probability density for any $x \in \mathcal{X}$, $T_t$ acts as a Markov operator. By the triangle inequality for integrals: \[ |(T_t f)(x)| \le \int_{\mathcal{X}} |f(y)| \pi_t(y \mid x) dy \le \|f\|_\infty \int_{\mathcal{X}} \pi_t(y \mid x) dy = \|f\|_\infty. \] Taking the supremum over $x$ yields $\|T_t f\|_\infty \le \|f\|_\infty$. The proof for $S_t$ is identical.
nodes.statement_short: Markov operator is non-expansive.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: (ii) Contraction on centered functions
nodes.statement:
(ii) By Lemma ef{lem:doeblin_from_bounds}, the conditional density admits the uniform lower bound $\pi_t(y \mid x) \ge \alpha 
u_t(y)$. This allows us to decompose the density as a convex combination: \[ \pi_t(y \mid x) = \alpha 
u_t(y) + (1-\alpha) r_{t,x}(y), \] where $r_{t,x}(y) :=  rac{\pi_t(y \mid x) - \alpha 
u_t(y)}{1-\alpha}$ is a valid residual probability density (non-negative and integrating to 1). Applying $T_t$ to a $
u_t$-centered function $b$: \[ (T_t b)(x) = \alpha \underbrace{\int_{\mathcal{X}} b(y) 
u_t(y) dy}_{= 0} + (1-\alpha) \int_{\mathcal{X}} b(y) r_{t,x}(y) dy. \] Taking the absolute value, we bound the remaining integral: \[ |(T_t b)(x)| \le (1-\alpha)\|b\|_\infty \int_{\mathcal{X}} r_{t,x}(y) dy = (1-\alpha)\|b\|_\infty. \] Since this holds for all $x$, taking the supremum yields $\|T_t b\|_\infty \le (1-\alpha)\|b\|_\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Doeblin decomposition gives contraction on centered functions.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: (iii) Composite contraction
nodes.statement: (iii) Applying the non-expansion of $S_t$ from part (i) sequentially with the contraction of $T_t$ on centered functions from part (ii), we immediately obtain: \[ \|S_t (T_t b)\|_\infty \le \|T_t b\|_\infty \le (1-\alpha)\|b\|_\infty, \] which confirms the strict contraction of the composite operator on the centered subspace.
nodes.statement_short: Combine (i) and (ii).
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Reduce to TV of kernels
nodes.statement: We prove the estimate for $T_t$ (the argument for $S_t$ is entirely symmetric). Fix $h \in L^\infty(\mathcal{X})$. By the definition of the conditional expectation, the difference is bounded by the total variation (TV) distance between the conditional kernels: \begin{equation} \|(T_r - T_t)h\|_\infty \le \|h\|_\infty \sup_{x \in \mathcal{X}} \|\pi_r(\cdot \mid x) - \pi_t(\cdot \mid x)\|_{\mathrm{TV}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Operator difference bounded by TV of conditional kernels.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Isolate psi_t in the kernel
nodes.statement: Using the relative entropy tilting formulation $\pi_t(x,y) = \pi'(x,y) \exp(\varphi_t(x) + \psi_t(y))$, the potential $\varphi_t(x)$ acts purely as a normalization factor for fixed $x$. Thus, the conditional density simplifies to: \[ \pi_t(y \mid x) = \frac{\pi'(x,y) \exp(\psi_t(y))}{Z_t(x)}, \quad \text{where } Z_t(x) := \int_{\mathcal{X}} \pi'(x,z) \exp(\psi_t(z)) dz. \] Crucially, this isolates the time-dependence strictly to the potential $\psi_t$. Define the point-wise logarithmic difference between the kernels at times $r$ and $t$: \[ \Delta(x,y) := \log \pi_r(y \mid x) - \log \pi_t(y \mid x) = \big(\psi_r(y) - \psi_t(y)\big) - \big(\log Z_r(x) - \log Z_t(x)\big). \] By Proposition \ref{prop:pot_Lip_time_Linfty}, $\|\psi_r - \psi_t\|_\infty \le L_{\mathrm{pot}} |r - t|$. Consequently, the normalization term satisfies: \[ |\log Z_r(x) - \log Z_t(x)| = \left| \log \frac{\int \pi'(x,z) e^{\psi_r(z)} dz}{\int \pi'(x,z) e^{\psi_t(z)} dz} \right| \le \|\psi_r - \psi_t\|_\infty \le L_{\mathrm{pot}} |r - t|, \] where we invoked again the 1-Lipschitz property of the Log-Sum-Exp operator. Thus, the logarithmic difference is uniformly bounded: \[ |\Delta(x,y)| \le \|\psi_r - \psi_t\|_\infty + |\log Z_r(x) - \log Z_t(x)| \le 2 L_{\mathrm{pot}} |r - t|. \]
nodes.statement_short: Log-difference of kernels bounded via time-Lipschitz potentials.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: TV bound and conclusion
nodes.statement: Let $\delta := 2 L_{\mathrm{pot}} |r - t|$. Using the identity $\|\pi_r - \pi_t\|_{\mathrm{TV}} = \frac{1}{2} \int |e^{\Delta} - 1| \pi_t dy$ and the elementary inequality $|e^\Delta - 1| \le |\Delta| e^{|\Delta|} \le \delta e^\delta$, we obtain: \[ \|\pi_r(\cdot \mid x) - \pi_t(\cdot \mid x)\|_{\mathrm{TV}} \le \frac{1}{2} \delta e^\delta = L_{\mathrm{pot}} |r - t| \exp(2 L_{\mathrm{pot}} |r - t|). \] Since $|r - t| \le 1$, the exponential term is bounded by $e^{2 L_{\mathrm{pot}}}$. Taking the supremum over $x$ yields: \[ \sup_{x \in \mathcal{X}} \|\pi_r(\cdot \mid x) - \pi_t(\cdot \mid x)\|_{\mathrm{TV}} \le \big( L_{\mathrm{pot}} e^{2 L_{\mathrm{pot}}} \big) |r - t|. \] Combining this with \eqref{eq:Tdiff_TV_final} concludes the proof, explicitly giving $L_{\mathrm{op}} := L_{\mathrm{pot}} e^{2 L_{\mathrm{pot}}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Exponential inequality gives TV bound; conclude.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Setup
nodes.statement: This proof uses the uniform $C^2$ spatial regularity from Lemma~\ref{lem:density_bounds} and the time-Lipschitz regularity of the marginal scores from Lemma~\ref{lem:temporal_marginal_regularity} (Part~2).
nodes.statement_short: Uses spatial and temporal marginal regularity.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Spatial bounds
nodes.statement:
We detail the estimates for $\zeta_t$; identical arguments hold for $\eta_t$. By the continuity equation, the forcing term is given by:  egin{equation} \zeta_t = -
abla \cdot u_t - u_t \cdot 
abla \log \mu_t. \end{equation} By Assumption ef{ass:velocity_regularity} and Lemma ef{lem:density_bounds}, $u_t, 
abla \cdot u_t$, and $
abla \log \mu_t$ are uniformly bounded. Applying the triangle inequality to \eqref{eq:zeta_def_explicit} yields the uniform $L^\infty$ bound: \[ \|\zeta_t\|_\infty \le \|
abla \cdot u_t\|_\infty + \|u_t\|_\infty \|
abla \log \mu_t\|_\infty \le C_{\mathrm{uv}} + C_{\mathrm{uv}} C_{\mathrm{score}}. \] For the spatial Lipschitz regularity, we use the product rule $\mathrm{Lip}_{\mathcal{X}}(fg) \le \|f\|_\infty \mathrm{Lip}_{\mathcal{X}}(g) + \|g\|_\infty \mathrm{Lip}_{\mathcal{X}}(f)$. Applying this to \eqref{eq:zeta_def_explicit} gives: \[ \mathrm{Lip}_{\mathcal{X}}(\zeta_t) \le \mathrm{Lip}_{\mathcal{X}}(
abla \cdot u_t) + \|u_t\|_\infty \mathrm{Lip}_{\mathcal{X}}(
abla \log \mu_t) + \|
abla \log \mu_t\|_\infty \mathrm{Lip}_{\mathcal{X}}(u_t). \] Since $u_t \in C^2(\mathcal{X})$ and $\log \mu_t \in C^2(\mathcal{X})$ (Lemma ef{lem:density_bounds}), all supremum norms and spatial Lipschitz constants on the right-hand side are bounded uniformly in $t$. Summing these spatial bounds for both $\zeta_t$ and $\eta_t$ establishes the existence of the single uniform constant $C_{\mathrm{force}} < \infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality and product rule bound $\zeta_t$ and its Lipschitz constant.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Temporal bounds
nodes.statement:
For the temporal regularity, we evaluate the difference $\zeta_r - \zeta_t$ via the decomposition: \[ \zeta_r - \zeta_t = -(
abla \cdot u_r - 
abla \cdot u_t) - (u_r - u_t) \cdot 
abla \log \mu_r - u_t \cdot (
abla \log \mu_r - 
abla \log \mu_t). \] By Assumption ef{ass:velocity_regularity}, the velocity field and its divergence are time-Lipschitz with constant $L_{\mathrm{uv}}$ (since $\|u_r-u_t\|_{C^1} \le L_{\mathrm{uv}}|r-t|$). Combining this with Lemma ef{lem:score_time_lip}, we take the $L^\infty$ norm and apply the triangle inequality:  egin{align*} \|\zeta_r - \zeta_t\|_\infty &\le \|
abla \cdot u_r - 
abla \cdot u_t\|_\infty + \|u_r - u_t\|_\infty \|
abla \log \mu_r\|_\infty + \|u_t\|_\infty \|
abla \log \mu_r - 
abla \log \mu_t\|_\infty \ &\le L_{\mathrm{uv}}|r-t| + L_{\mathrm{uv}}|r-t| C_{\mathrm{score}} + C_{\mathrm{uv}} L_{\mathrm{score}} |r-t|. \end{align*} Factoring out $|r-t|$, we define $L_{\mathrm{force}} := 2  ig( L_{\mathrm{uv}}(1 + C_{\mathrm{score}}) + C_{\mathrm{uv}} L_{\mathrm{score}}  ig)$ (to account for both $\zeta$ and $\eta$), which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Decompose $\zeta_r-\zeta_t$ and bound each term.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Perturbation identity
nodes.statement: For each $t \in [0,1]$, under the gauge $\int b_t \, d\nu_t = 0$, the tilting rate $b_t$ is the unique solution to the operator equation $(I - S_t T_t) b_t = \eta_t - S_t \zeta_t$. Correspondingly, $a_t = \zeta_t - T_t b_t$. Fix $r, t \in [0,1]$ and consider the difference $(I - S_r T_r)(b_r - b_t)$. By adding and subtracting $(I - S_r T_r)b_t$, we obtain the fundamental perturbation identity: \begin{equation} (I - S_r T_r)(b_r - b_t) = (\eta_r - \eta_t) - S_r(\zeta_r - \zeta_t) - (S_r - S_t) \zeta_t + S_r(T_r - T_t) b_t + (S_r - S_t) T_t b_t. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Write $b_t$ as solution of $(I-S_tT_t)b=\eta_t-S_t\zeta_t$ and derive the perturbation identity.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Invert with contraction
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{lem:Doeblin_centered_Linfty}, the composite operator $S_r T_r$ is a strict contraction on the $\nu_r$-centered subspace with $\|S_r T_r\| \le 1 - \alpha$. Thus, the operator $(I - S_r T_r)$ is invertible on this subspace, and its inverse is uniformly bounded by $\|(I - S_r T_r)^{-1}\| \le 1/\alpha$. Applying this to \eqref{eq:perturbation_identity} and invoking the non-expansivity $\|S_r\| \le 1$ from Lemma \ref{lem:Doeblin_centered_Linfty}: \begin{align} \|b_r - b_t\|_\infty \le \frac{1}{\alpha} \Big( & \|\eta_r - \eta_t\|_\infty + \|\zeta_r - \zeta_t\|_\infty + \|(S_r - S_t) \zeta_t\|_\infty \nonumber \\ & + \|(T_r - T_t) b_t\|_\infty + \|(S_r - S_t) T_t b_t\|_\infty \Big). \end{align} We bound each term in \eqref{eq:b_diff_expansion} using previously established regularities:
nodes.statement_short: Invert $(I-S_rT_r)$ with norm $1/\alpha$ and expand.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Forcing terms
nodes.statement: Forcing terms: By Lemma \ref{lem:forcing_regularity}, $\|\eta_r - \eta_t\|_\infty + \|\zeta_r - \zeta_t\|_\infty \le L_{\mathrm{force}} |r - t|$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound forcing differences.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Operator stability on zeta_t
nodes.statement: Operator stability on $\zeta_t$: By Lemma \ref{lem:operator_stability_Linfty}, $\|(S_r - S_t) \zeta_t\|_\infty \le L_{\mathrm{op}} \|\zeta_t\|_\infty |r - t| \le L_{\mathrm{op}} C_{\mathrm{force}} |r - t|$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $(S_r-S_t)\zeta_t$.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Operator stability on b_t
nodes.statement: Operator stability on $b_t$: By Proposition \ref{prop:ab_uniform_Linfty}, $\|b_t\|_\infty \le C_{ab}^\infty$. Thus, $\|(T_r - T_t) b_t\|_\infty \le L_{\mathrm{op}} C_{ab}^\infty |r - t|$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $(T_r-T_t)b_t$.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Composite stability
nodes.statement: Composite stability: Since $\|T_t b_t\|_\infty \le \|b_t\|_\infty \le C_{ab}^\infty$, by Lemma \ref{lem:operator_stability_Linfty} and Proposition \ref{prop:ab_uniform_Linfty}, the final term satisfies $\|(S_r - S_t) T_t b_t\|_\infty \le L_{\mathrm{op}} C_{ab}^\infty |r - t|$.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $(S_r-S_t)T_tb_t$.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Sum for b
nodes.statement: Summing these estimates yields $\|b_r - b_t\|_\infty \le L_b |r - t|$ with $L_b := \frac{1}{\alpha}(L_{\mathrm{force}} + L_{\mathrm{op}} C_{\mathrm{force}} + 2 L_{\mathrm{op}} C_{ab}^\infty)$.
nodes.statement_short: Collect terms into $L_b$.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Bound for a and conclude
nodes.statement: Using the relation $a_t = \zeta_t - T_t b_t$, we decompose the difference as: \begin{align*} \|a_r - a_t\|_\infty &= \|(\zeta_r - \zeta_t) - (T_r b_r - T_t b_t)\|_\infty \\ &\le \|\zeta_r - \zeta_t\|_\infty + \|(T_r - T_t) b_r\|_\infty + \|T_t(b_r - b_t)\|_\infty \\ &\le L_{\mathrm{force}} |r - t| + L_{\mathrm{op}} C_{ab}^\infty |r - t| + L_b |r - t| =: L_a |r - t|. \end{align*} Defining $L_{ab} := L_a + L_b$ concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Bound $a_r-a_t$ via $a=\zeta-Tb$ and conclude.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Define exponents
nodes.statement: Let $G(x,y) := \int_t^{t+\delta} F_r(x,y)\,dr$ and $\bar{G}(x,y) := \delta F_t(x,y)$ denote the exact and frozen exponents, with $Z := \int e^G\,d\pi_t$ and $\bar{Z} := \int e^{\bar{G}}\,d\pi_t$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce exact and frozen exponents and normalizers.
nodes.section: G.1 Stability Analysis of the Coupling Measure

nodes.name: Bound the exponent difference
nodes.statement: \textbf{Bound the exponent difference.} By Corollary~\ref{cor:F_regularity}, $\|F_r - F_t\|_\infty \le L_{ab}|r - t|$. Therefore the pointwise exponent difference satisfies: \[ \|\Delta\|_\infty := \left\| G - \bar{G} \right\|_\infty = \left\| \int_t^{t+\delta} (F_r - F_t)\,dr \right\|_\infty \le \int_t^{t+\delta} L_{ab}(r-t)\,dr = \tfrac{1}{2}L_{ab}\delta^2. \] Set $\varepsilon := \|\Delta\|_\infty \le \tfrac{1}{2}L_{ab}\delta^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Exponent difference at most $L_{ab}\delta^2/2$.
nodes.section: G.1 Stability Analysis of the Coupling Measure

nodes.name: Stability of Gibbs measures
nodes.statement: \textbf{Stability of Gibbs measures.} Since $e^G = e^{\bar{G}} \cdot e^{\Delta}$, the Radon-Nikodym derivative of $\pi_{t+\delta}$ with respect to $\bar{\pi}_{t+\delta}$ is $\frac{d\pi_{t+\delta}}{d\bar{\pi}_{t+\delta}} = e^{\Delta} \cdot \frac{\bar{Z}}{Z}.$ By the 1-Lipschitz property of $\log\int e^{(\cdot)}\,d\pi_t$, \[ \left|\log \frac{Z}{\bar{Z}}\right| = \left|\log\frac{\int e^G d\pi_t}{\int e^{\bar{G}} d\pi_t}\right| \le \|G - \bar{G}\|_\infty = \varepsilon. \] Hence $|\log(d\pi_{t+\delta}/d\bar{\pi}_{t+\delta})| = |\Delta - \log(Z/\bar{Z})| \le 2\varepsilon$ uniformly. Using the identity $2\|P - Q\|_{TV} = \mathbb{E}_Q[|dP/dQ - 1|]$ and the elementary bound $|e^u - 1| \le |u|\,e^{|u|}$: \[ E_{\mathrm{local}} = \|\pi_{t+\delta} - \bar{\pi}_{t+\delta}\|_{TV} \le \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathbb{E}_{\bar{\pi}_{t+\delta}}\!\left[\left|e^{\Delta - \log(Z/\bar{Z})} - 1\right|\right] \le \varepsilon\,e^{2\varepsilon} \le \tfrac{1}{2}L_{ab}\delta^2 \cdot e^{L_{ab}\delta^2}. \] For $\delta \le 1$, set $C_1 := \tfrac{1}{2}L_{ab}e^{L_{ab}}$ so that $E_{\mathrm{local}} \le C_1\delta^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Bounded log Radon-Nikodym derivative gives the TV bound.
nodes.section: G.1 Stability Analysis of the Coupling Measure

nodes.name: TV of the two tilted measures
nodes.statement: Recall that $\bar{\pi}_{t+\delta}$ and $\tilde{\pi}_{t+\delta}$ are obtained by tilting $\pi_t$ and $\tilde{\pi}_t$ respectively with the same frozen weight $\exp(\delta F_t)$. By the definition of the Total Variation distance: \begin{equation} 2 E_{\mathrm{prop}} = \int_{\mathcal{X}^2} \left| \frac{e^{\delta F_t(x,y)} d\pi_t(x,y)}{\int e^{\delta F_t} d\pi_t} - \frac{e^{\delta F_t(x,y)} d\tilde{\pi}_t(x,y)}{\int e^{\delta F_t} d\tilde{\pi}_t} \right|. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Write $2E_{prop}$ as an integral of the difference of normalized tilts.
nodes.section: G.1 Stability Analysis of the Coupling Measure

nodes.name: Triangle split
nodes.statement: Using the triangle inequality, the integrand is bounded as: \begin{align*} \left| \frac{e^{\delta F_t} d\pi_t}{\int e^{\delta F_t} d\pi_t} - \frac{e^{\delta F_t} d\tilde{\pi}_t}{\int e^{\delta F_t} d\tilde{\pi}_t} \right| \le \underbrace{\frac{e^{\delta F_t}}{\int e^{\delta F_t} d\pi_t} |d\pi_t - d\tilde{\pi}_t|}_{(\mathrm{I})} + \underbrace{e^{\delta F_t} d\tilde{\pi}_t \left| \frac{1}{\int e^{\delta F_t} d\pi_t} - \frac{1}{\int e^{\delta F_t} d\tilde{\pi}_t} \right|}_{(\mathrm{II})}. \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Split integrand into terms (I) and (II).
nodes.section: G.1 Stability Analysis of the Coupling Measure

nodes.name: Bound term (I)
nodes.statement: Integrating term $(\mathrm{I})$ over $\mathcal{X}^2$: \[ \int(\mathrm{I}) \le \frac{\|e^{\delta F_t}\|_\infty}{\int e^{\delta F_t} d\pi_t}\cdot 2\varepsilon_t. \]
nodes.statement_short: Term (I) bounded by $2\varepsilon_t$ times sup ratio.
nodes.section: G.1 Stability Analysis of the Coupling Measure

nodes.name: Bound term (II)
nodes.statement: For term $(\mathrm{II})$, write $D_\pi := \int e^{\delta F_t} d\pi_t$ and $D_{\tilde\pi} := \int e^{\delta F_t} d\tilde\pi_t$. Since $\pi_t$ and $\tilde\pi_t$ are both probability measures, $\int 1\,d(\tilde\pi_t - \pi_t) = 0$, so \[ |D_{\tilde\pi} - D_\pi| = \left|\int \bigl(e^{\delta F_t}-1\bigr)\,d(\tilde\pi_t-\pi_t)\right| \le \|e^{\delta F_t}-1\|_\infty \cdot 2\varepsilon_t \le \bigl(e^{\delta C_{ab}^\infty}-1\bigr)\cdot 2\varepsilon_t. \]
nodes.statement_short: Difference of normalizers bounded via TV.
nodes.section: G.1 Stability Analysis of the Coupling Measure

nodes.name: Sum contributions
nodes.statement: Summing both contributions: \begin{align*} 2 E_{\mathrm{prop}} \le 2e^{2\delta C_{ab}^\infty}\varepsilon_t + 2\bigl(e^{2\delta C_{ab}^\infty}-e^{\delta C_{ab}^\infty}\bigr)\varepsilon_t = 2\bigl(2e^{2\delta C_{ab}^\infty}-e^{\delta C_{ab}^\infty}\bigr)\varepsilon_t, \end{align*} so $E_{\mathrm{prop}} \le \bigl(2e^{2\delta C_{ab}^\infty}-e^{\delta C_{ab}^\infty}\bigr)\varepsilon_t$. Note that this bound is tight at $\delta=0$: $2\cdot 1 - 1 = 1$, recovering $E_{\mathrm{prop}} \le \varepsilon_t$ exactly.
nodes.statement_short: Combine (I) and (II).
nodes.section: G.1 Stability Analysis of the Coupling Measure

nodes.name: Mean value bound
nodes.statement: Let $f(\delta) := 2e^{2\delta C_{ab}^\infty} - e^{\delta C_{ab}^\infty}$. Then $f(0)=1$ and $f'(\delta) = 4C_{ab}^\infty e^{2\delta C_{ab}^\infty} - C_{ab}^\infty e^{\delta C_{ab}^\infty} \le 4C_{ab}^\infty e^{2C_{ab}^\infty}$ for $\delta\in[0,1]$. By the mean value theorem, $f(\delta) \le 1 + 4C_{ab}^\infty e^{2C_{ab}^\infty}\,\delta$, so defining $C_2 := 4\,C_{ab}^\infty e^{2C_{ab}^\infty}$: \begin{equation} E_{\mathrm{prop}} \le (1 + C_2 \delta)\,\varepsilon_t. \end{equation} This completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Mean value theorem gives $1+C_2\delta$.
nodes.section: G.1 Stability Analysis of the Coupling Measure

nodes.name: Zero initial error
nodes.statement: Consider the sequence of errors $\{\varepsilon_{t_k}\}_{k=0}^N$ where $t_k = k\delta$. The algorithm is supposed to be initialized with $\tilde{\pi}_0 = \pi_0 = \pi'$ (both coincide with the reference coupling by construction), so $\varepsilon_0 = \|\pi_0 - \tilde{\pi}_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}} = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Exact initialization gives $\varepsilon_0=0$.
nodes.section: G.1 Stability Analysis of the Coupling Measure

nodes.name: Iterate the recurrence
nodes.statement: By iterating the recurrence from Corollary \ref{cor:error_recursion} starting from $\varepsilon_0 = 0$: \begin{equation*} \varepsilon_{t_k} \le C_1 \delta^2 \sum_{j=0}^{k-1} (1 + C_2 \delta)^j = C_1 \delta^2 \frac{(1 + C_2 \delta)^k - 1}{(1 + C_2 \delta) - 1}. \end{equation*} Simplifying the denominator gives: \begin{equation*} \varepsilon_{t_k} \le \frac{C_1 \delta}{C_2} \left[ (1 + C_2 \delta)^k - 1 \right]. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Unroll the recursion into a geometric sum.
nodes.section: G.1 Stability Analysis of the Coupling Measure

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Using the bound $(1 + C_2 \delta)^k \le e^{k C_2 \delta}$, and setting $k=N=1/\delta$, we obtain: \begin{equation*} \varepsilon_1 \le \frac{C_1}{C_2} (e^{C_2} - 1) \delta, \end{equation*} which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Exponential bound with $k=N$ gives $O(\delta)$.
nodes.section: G.1 Stability Analysis of the Coupling Measure

nodes.name: Integrability
nodes.statement: We first establish the conditional bounds for the vector field. The time derivative is given by $\dot{I}_s = (Y - X) + \Xi \frac{1-2s}{2\sqrt{s(1-s)}}$. Since $\Xi \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2 I)$, its first moment is finite ($\mathbb{E}[\|\Xi\|] < \infty$). Because $X, Y$ reside in the compact space $\mathcal{X}$, we trivially have $\mathbb{E}[\|\dot{I}_s\|] < \infty$. This $L^1(\mathbb{P})$ integrability guarantees the existence of the conditional expectation.
nodes.statement_short: $\dot I_s$ is integrable.
nodes.section: G.2 Stability Analysis of the Regression Field

nodes.name: Explicit conditional field and bound
nodes.statement: Conditioning on $I_s = z, X=x, Y=y$ fixes the noise realization as $\Xi = \frac{z - (1-s)x - sy}{\sqrt{s(1-s)}}$. Substituting this yields the explicit continuous conditional vector field: \begin{equation*} v_s(z \mid x,y) = (y - x) + \frac{1-2s}{2s(1-s)} \big(z - ((1-s)x + sy)\big) = (y - x) + \frac{1-2s}{2s(1-s)} \big(z - m_s(x, y)\big). \end{equation*} Since $x, y, z \in \mathcal{X}$ are within the compact state space, all spatial distances are bounded. For any fixed $s \in (0,1)$, the denominator $s(1-s)$ is strictly positive. Applying the triangle inequality yields a finite deterministic bound $\sup_{x,y,z \in \mathcal{X}} \|v_s(z \mid x,y)\| \le \mathrm{diam}(\mathcal{X}) + \frac{|1-2s|}{2s(1-s)} \sup_{x,y,z \in \mathcal{X}} \|z - m_s(x,y)\| =: C_v(s) < \infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Compute $v_s$ explicitly and bound it on the compact domain.
nodes.section: G.2 Stability Analysis of the Regression Field

nodes.name: Density lower bound
nodes.statement: Next, we address the non-degenerate marginal densities. The Gaussian transition density $p(z \mid x,y) = \mathcal{N}(z ; m_s(x,y), \sigma_s^2 I)$ is continuous and strictly positive, where the variance schedule is $\sigma_s^2 = \sigma^2 s(1-s)$. For a fixed $s \in (0,1)$, on the compact domain $\mathcal{X}^3$, it attains a strictly positive minimum $p_{\min}(s) > 0$. By Proposition \ref{prop:ab_uniform_Linfty}, the joint density admits a uniform lower bound $\rho_{\min} > 0$. Integrating out the joint coupling explicitly provides the marginalized lower bound $p_{\pi_t}(z; s) \ge p_{\min}(s) \cdot \rho_{\min} \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{X}^2) =: \underline{p}(s) > 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Positive Gaussian density and coupling lower bound give $\underline p(s)$.
nodes.section: G.2 Stability Analysis of the Regression Field

nodes.name: Shorthand
nodes.statement: Fix $z \in \mathcal{X}$ and $s \in (0,1)$. Set $G := \int_t^{t+\delta} F_r\,dr$ and $\bar{G} := \delta F_t$. Define the shorthand \[ \mathcal{N}(\mu, W) := \int v_s(z|x,y)\,p(z|x,y)\,W(x,y)\,d\mu(x,y), \quad \mathcal{D}(\mu, W) := \int p(z|x,y)\,W(x,y)\,d\mu(x,y) \] so that $\beta_s^t(z) = \mathcal{N}(\pi_t, e^G)/\mathcal{D}(\pi_t, e^G)$ and $\tilde{\beta}_s^t(z) = \mathcal{N}(\tilde{\pi}_t, e^{\bar{G}})/\mathcal{D}(\tilde{\pi}_t, e^{\bar{G}})$.
nodes.statement_short: Write both fields as numerator/denominator ratios.
nodes.section: G.2 Stability Analysis of the Regression Field

nodes.name: Fractional perturbation
nodes.statement: Applying the fractional perturbation identity $\bigl|\tfrac{A}{B} - \tfrac{a}{b}\bigr| \le \tfrac{|A-a|}{B} + \tfrac{|a|\,|B-b|}{Bb}$ with $(A,B) = (\mathcal{N}(\pi_t,e^G), \mathcal{D}(\pi_t,e^G))$ and $(a,b) = (\mathcal{N}(\tilde{\pi}_t,e^{\bar{G}}), \mathcal{D}(\tilde{\pi}_t,e^{\bar{G}}))$, and using the lower bound $\mathcal{D}(\pi_t, e^G) \ge \underline{p}(s)\,e^{-\delta C_{ab}^\infty}$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:beta_environment_regularity}: \begin{align*} |\beta_s^t(z) - \tilde{\beta}_s^t(z)| \le \frac{|\mathcal{N}(\pi_t,e^G) - \mathcal{N}(\tilde{\pi}_t,e^{\bar{G}})|}{\mathcal{D}(\pi_t,e^G)} + \frac{C_v(s)\,|\mathcal{D}(\pi_t,e^G) - \mathcal{D}(\tilde{\pi}_t,e^{\bar{G}})|}{\mathcal{D}(\pi_t,e^G)\,\mathcal{D}(\tilde{\pi}_t,e^{\bar{G}})}. \end{align*} For each of these two differences, apply the triangle inequality by splitting at $(\pi_t, e^{\bar{G}})$: \begin{align*} |\mathcal{N}(\pi_t,e^G) - \mathcal{N}(\tilde{\pi}_t,e^{\bar{G}})| &\le \underbrace{|\mathcal{N}(\pi_t,e^G) - \mathcal{N}(\pi_t,e^{\bar{G}})|}_{\text{weight discrepancy}} + \underbrace{|\mathcal{N}(\pi_t,e^{\bar{G}}) - \mathcal{N}(\tilde{\pi}_t,e^{\bar{G}})|}_{\text{measure discrepancy}}, \end{align*} and similarly for $\mathcal{D}$.
nodes.statement_short: Fractional perturbation and split into weight and measure discrepancies.
nodes.section: G.2 Stability Analysis of the Regression Field

nodes.name: Weight discrepancy
nodes.statement: \textbf{Weight discrepancy.} Since $|e^G - e^{\bar{G}}| \le e^{\delta C_{ab}^\infty}\|G - \bar{G}\|_\infty$ and $\|G - \bar{G}\|_\infty \le \tfrac{1}{2}L_{ab}\delta^2$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:local_error_tv}, Step~1): \[ |\mathcal{N}(\pi_t,e^G) - \mathcal{N}(\pi_t,e^{\bar{G}})| \le C_v(s)\,e^{\delta C_{ab}^\infty} \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}L_{ab}\delta^2, \] and the same bound holds for $|\mathcal{D}(\pi_t,e^G) - \mathcal{D}(\pi_t,e^{\bar{G}})|$.
nodes.statement_short: Weight discrepancy is $O(\delta^2)$.
nodes.section: G.2 Stability Analysis of the Regression Field

nodes.name: Measure discrepancy
nodes.statement: \textbf{Measure discrepancy.} By the TV duality bound for signed integrals and the uniform weight bound $\|e^{\bar{G}}\|_\infty \le e^{\delta C_{ab}^\infty}$: \[ |\mathcal{N}(\pi_t,e^{\bar{G}}) - \mathcal{N}(\tilde{\pi}_t,e^{\bar{G}})| \le 2\,C_v(s)\,e^{\delta C_{ab}^\infty}\,\varepsilon_t, \] and similarly $|\mathcal{D}(\pi_t,e^{\bar{G}}) - \mathcal{D}(\tilde{\pi}_t,e^{\bar{G}})| \le 2\,e^{\delta C_{ab}^\infty}\,\varepsilon_t$, where $\varepsilon_t := \|\pi_t - \tilde{\pi}_t\|_{\mathrm{TV}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Measure discrepancy bounded by $\varepsilon_t$ via TV duality.
nodes.section: G.2 Stability Analysis of the Regression Field

nodes.name: Combining
nodes.statement: \textbf{Combining.} Substituting into the fractional perturbation bound and absorbing constants: \begin{align*} |\beta_s^t(z) - \tilde{\beta}_s^t(z)| &\le \underbrace{\left(\frac{C_v(s)}{\underline{p}(s)} + \frac{C_v(s)}{\underline{p}(s)^2}\right) e^{2\delta C_{ab}^\infty} \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}L_{ab}\delta^2}_{=:\,K_1(s)\,\delta^2} + \underbrace{2C_v(s)\!\left(\frac{1}{\underline{p}(s)} + \frac{1}{\underline{p}(s)^2}\right) e^{2\delta C_{ab}^\infty}\,\varepsilon_t}_{=:\,K_2(s)\,\varepsilon_t}. \end{align*} Substituting the global convergence bound $\varepsilon_t \le C_{\mathrm{global}}\,\delta$ yields the pointwise error bound: \begin{equation} \|\beta_s^t - \tilde{\beta}_s^t\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal{X})} \le K_1(s)\,\delta^2 + K_2(s)\,C_{\mathrm{global}}\,\delta \le C_\beta(s)\,\delta, \end{equation} where $C_\beta(s) := K_1(s) + K_2(s)\,C_{\mathrm{global}}$ is deterministic and strictly finite for any fixed $s \in (0,1)$, which completes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Combine and use the global TV bound to get $C_\beta(s)\delta$.
nodes.section: G.2 Stability Analysis of the Regression Field

nodes.name: Fix b and set up objective
nodes.statement: We verify the equivalence for the $a$-update; the $b$-update follows symmetrically. Fix $b = b_t$ and consider the quadratic objective \[ \mathcal{L}(a) := \mathbb{E}_{\pi_t}\!\Big[\big(a(X)+b_t(Y)-\zeta_t(X)\big)^2\Big]. \] This is a convex quadratic functional in $a \in L^2(\mu_t)$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix $b=b_t$; the $a$-objective is convex quadratic.
nodes.section: D Variational Characterization of the Tilting Dynamics

nodes.name: First-order condition
nodes.statement: Its Fr\'echet derivative in the direction of any test function $p \in L^2(\mu_t)$ is \[ \frac{d}{d\xi}\mathcal{L}(a+\xi p)\Big|_{\xi=0} = 2\,\mathbb{E}_{\pi_t}\!\Big[p(X)\big(a(X)+b_t(Y)-\zeta_t(X)\big)\Big]. \] Setting this to zero and using the tower property $\mathbb{E}_{\pi_t}[b_t(Y)p(X)] = \mathbb{E}_{\mu_t}[p(X)(T_t b_t)(X)]$, we obtain $\mathbb{E}_{\mu_t}[p(X)(a(X)+(T_t b_t)(X)-\zeta_t(X))]=0$ for all $p$, hence $a + T_t b_t = \zeta_t$ $\mu_t$-a.s., which is the first equation of \eqref{eq:app_linear_system_ab}.
nodes.statement_short: Zero Frechet derivative plus tower property gives $a+T_tb_t=\zeta_t$.
nodes.section: D Variational Characterization of the Tilting Dynamics

nodes.name: Symmetric b-update
nodes.statement: An identical computation on $\mathcal{L}(b) := \mathbb{E}_{\pi_t}[(a_t(X)+b(Y)-\eta_t(Y))^2]$ yields $b + S_t a_t = \eta_t$ $\nu_t$-a.s.
nodes.statement_short: Same computation for $b$.
nodes.section: D Variational Characterization of the Tilting Dynamics

nodes.name: Rademacher bound
nodes.statement: By Proposition \ref{prop:pot_Lip_time_Linfty}, each potential $\varphi_t$ (resp.\ $\psi_t$) is time-Lipschitz with individual constant $L_{\mathrm{pot}}/2$. Therefore, by Rademacher's theorem \citep[Theorem~3.1.2]{evans2015measure}, their time derivatives $a_t = \dot\varphi_t$ and $b_t = \dot\psi_t$ exist for a.e.\ $t \in [0,1]$ (applied pointwise in $x$ to the scalar Lipschitz function $t\mapsto\varphi_t(x)$) and are essentially bounded: \[ \|a_t\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal{X})} \le \tfrac{L_{\mathrm{pot}}}{2} \quad \text{and} \quad \|b_t\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal{X})} \le \tfrac{L_{\mathrm{pot}}}{2}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Time-Lipschitz potentials have bounded a.e. time derivatives.
nodes.section: F.1 Uniform Boundedness via Relative Potentials

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Setting $C_{ab}^\infty := L_{\mathrm{pot}}$ bounds the sum of their norms. The complete chain of inequalities then follows directly from the triangle inequality $\|a_t(x) + b_t(y)\|_\infty \le \|a_t\|_\infty + \|b_t\|_\infty \le C_{ab}^\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality gives the bound.
nodes.section: F.1 Uniform Boundedness via Relative Potentials

nodes.name: Reduce to PMI ratio
nodes.statement_short: Minorization reduces to bounding the pointwise mutual information ratio.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Bound numerator and denominator
nodes.statement: We can bound the numerator from below and the denominator from above using our established uniform bounds: By Assumption \ref{ass:coupling_regularity}, $\|\log \pi'\|_\infty \le C_\mathrm{OT}$, implying $\pi'(x,y) \ge e^{-C_\mathrm{OT}}$. By Lemma \ref{lem:phi_psi_regularity}, $\varphi_t(x) \ge -C_\infty$ and $\psi_t(y) \ge -C_\infty$. By Lemma \ref{lem:density_bounds}, the marginal densities are strictly bounded above by constants $C_{\mu}^{\max}$ and $C_{\nu}^{\max}$.
nodes.statement_short: Collect lower and upper bounds from assumptions and lemmas.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Substituting these bounds into \eqref{eq:pmi_ratio} directly yields the uniform lower bound: \[ \frac{\pi_t(y \mid x)}{\nu_t(y)} \ge \frac{\exp(-C_\mathrm{OT}) \cdot \exp(-2C_\infty)}{C_{\mu}^{\max} C_{\nu}^{\max}} =: \alpha. \] By the symmetric structure of the joint density in \eqref{eq:pmi_ratio}, the exact same lower bound applies to the inverse conditional ratio $\pi_t(x \mid y) / \mu_t(x)$, completing the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute to get $\alpha$; symmetric for the other conditional.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Temporal regularity
nodes.statement: The temporal regularity is immediate from Proposition \ref{prop:ab_stability}.
nodes.statement_short: Time part follows from Proposition F.8.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Quotient form of T_t b_t
nodes.statement: For spatial regularity, fix $t \in [0,1]$. By Lemma \ref{lem:forcing_regularity}, $\zeta_t$ is uniformly Lipschitz. For the operator term $T_t b_t(x) = \int b_t(y) \pi_t(y \mid x) dy$, we substitute the conditional density: \[ T_t b_t(x) = \frac{\int b_t(y) \pi'(x,y) e^{\psi_t(y)} dy}{\int \pi'(x,z) e^{\psi_t(z)} dz}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Write $T_tb_t$ as a quotient with the reference kernel.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization

nodes.name: Spatial Lipschitz
nodes.statement: Under Assumption \ref{ass:coupling_regularity}, the reference kernel $\pi'(x,y)$ is Lipschitz in $x$. Since $b_t$ and $\psi_t$ are uniformly bounded (Lemma \ref{lem:phi_psi_regularity} and Proposition \ref{prop:ab_uniform_Linfty}), and the denominator is bounded away from zero by Doeblin minorization, the quotient $T_t b_t$ is spatially Lipschitz. A symmetric argument for $S_t a_t$ ensures the uniform spatial Lipschitzness of $b_t$, and thus of $F_t$.
nodes.statement_short: Lipschitz kernel, bounded numerator, Doeblin-bounded denominator give Lipschitz $F_t$.
nodes.section: F.2 Spatiotemporal Stability and Doeblin Minorization
